description: In 1862 date of application of FYM, rape cake, PKNaMg and autumn N not recorded. Assumed before seed sown on 25/10/1861.

In 1889 and 1890 many plots were sub-divided into four. Two sub-plots were sown in nine wide rows, allowing inter-row cultivation to control weeds, two were sown with the usual 18 row spacing. Yields shown here are means from the usual 18 row sub-plots, data from the wide row sub-plots has been excluded.

In 1856 sub-plot 3a (1/3 of plot 3) excluded from the mean as fertilizer N (96kgN/ha as ammonium sulphate) applied that year only. Yields in subsequent years didn't show an increase, so included in mean.

In 1901 most plots receiving N were divided into three subplots, with one (TM) receiving N as bicarbonate of ammonia, rather than the usual ammonium sulphate. Data from sub-plot TM is excluded from the mean yields shown here.
In 1892, plot 15 was havested as four sub-plots (15aB, 15aT, 15bB, 15bT). There was little difference between the four sub-plots, so data shown is the  mean of all four.

Yields are shown for sub-plots 9a and 9b, 1852-1893, as they received different fertilizer treatments. Plot 9a yielded around 50% more than 9b. From 1894 9a and 9b received the same fertilizer treatment, but they are still shown as separate plots. They were combined as one plot in 1899.

Yields are shown for sub-plots 15a and 15b 1852-72, as they received different fertilizer treatments. The yield difference was less than 5%. From 1873 they received the same fertilizer treatment, so mean yields are shown.

In 1861 plot 17a was unequally divided into 17a-1 and 17a-2, due to concerns that the fertilizer applied to plot 16b was influencing yield on part of plot 17a.  Yields shown here are weighted means, according to the area harvested.

Plot 9b was unequally divided into 9b-1 and 9b-2 in 1883-8 and 1891-2. This was due to concerns that the fertilizer applied to 9a was influencing yield in 9b-2. Data shown here is weighted mean for 9b, based on the number of rows harvested from 9b-1 and 9b-2.

Strip 10b was unequally divided into 10b-1 and 10b-2 in 1872, 1878, 1879, 1883-1893, due to concerns that fertilizer from strip 11 was influencing yield on strip 10b. Data shown here is the weighted mean, based on the number of rows harvested. Strip 10b yielded around 13% more than strip 10a, 1852-1894. This compared with less than 5% difference in yield between all other 'a' and 'b' halves which had received the same fertilizer treatments.
Strip 19 was smaller than other strips (0.12ha) until 1894, when its size was partly increased at the west end by bringing in an adjacent unmanured area.
In 1904 the whole of strip 19 was increased to the standard size (0.202ha) by bringing in an adjacent area. This was part unmanured and part headland.
Plot 20. No yields recorded 1912 and 1914 as there was no crop.
In 1904 most strips were divided in half longitudinally, one half was cropped, and other was bare fallowed
In 1905 most strips were divided in half longitudinally, one half was bare fallowed (which had been cropped the previous year) and one cropped (which had been bare fallowed the previous year).

In 1906 data shown for strip 11 is mean of two sub-plots. In 1905 many strips were divided into two (see note 15). Fallow increased yields in 1906, the largest difference was in Strip 11, which was harvested as two halves (11a and 11b) this year only.
In 1915 no N was applied in autumn, all applied in the spring, except strip 15 which received no N. No FYM or PKNaMg applied. Rape cake applied as usual.
No rape cake applied to plot 19 1917-1920
No K, Na*, Mg* applied 1917-1919
Cropped area for strip 20 in 1924 is shown as 0.101 ha in 1924 yield sheet. This is proabably an error, as in all other years it is shown as 0.0675
Plot 2.1, started in 1885. Also known as strip 2a.
Plot 2.2, originally strip 2 (started in 1843), but renamed 2.2 in 1885 when plot 2.1 was started. Also known as strip 2b.

In 1867-1879, the straw which grew on strip 5a-8a, 11a-14a, 17a and 18a in the previous season was chopped and incorporated. No straw was incorporated on the b strips. Strips 17a and 18a only received straw in the years when N was not applied. Overall, the difference in yield was less than 1%, except in plots 17 and 18, where straw incorporation reduced yield by an average of 9%.
